Document: MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

Findings:
[{"id":"f-lol-cap-7df8de07","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees \"paid or payable\" and USD 1,000,000 (§21.1); \"Fees\" (§1.5) is a substantive base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory. §21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages. §21.3 places outside the cap breaches of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's payment of undisputed Fees is not \"damages\" subject to the cap. §21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited, and §18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No one-sided or hidden liability limitation appears elsewhere in the document. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-986b3296","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets the preferred position in full. 24.1 gives Customer an unrestricted right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor without Vendor consent (notice only). 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness standard qualified by capability/financial standing), and never to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, and requires cooperation with successor administration. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1: by its terms it applies only to \"other assignments\" — i.e. those outside the carve-outs in 24.1 and 24.2 — and applies a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard. Section 13.3 is consistent, permitting transfer of licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-a49b15e6","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"Section 7.2 (the first clause numbered 7.2) conditions our ability to engage any other provider on first disclosing a competing offer and giving Vendor the chance to match it — a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal binding Customer for the whole term, with no defined product category, no 12-month limit and no exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates. It therefore fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. Flipping the mandatory operator so that Customer is not required to disclose or match delivers the preferred position (no exclusivity and no sole-supplier obligation on Customer) with the smallest operative change, and removes the conflict with Section 12.3. Exclusivity running in our favour is untouched.","proposal":"Turn Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation into an express no-obligation, removing the de facto exclusivity/ROFR on Customer.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-ld-0fbf9b06","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"termination fee\", \"accelerate\", and all termination provisions (§§ 8–10, 27.3) return no amount payable by Customer as liquidated damages, a penalty, an early-termination fee, or a minimum charge on termination. The only \"penalty\" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; and § 24.4 bars fee acceleration on Customer change of control. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. The take-or-pay minimum commitment in § 2.1 is the closest economic analogue but is a purchase commitment rather than a liquidated-damages or penalty mechanic and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule; we do not flag it twice here. Noted for context only: the body contains no service-credit regime, which is referenced to the service-level exhibit under § 2.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-b9030008","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"The grant clause meets the preferred position on all material terms: § 13.1 extends the subscription licence to Customer's Affiliates and to contractors acting on their behalf (and to Authorized Users); § 13.2 makes paid-up software and Vendor Technology (including material embedded in a Deliverable) perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free and fully paid for Customer and its Affiliates, with contractor support permitted; and § 13.3 allows transfer to an Affiliate or successor on a permitted assignment and bars Vendor revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity. No \"revocable at Vendor's discretion\" or affiliate/contractor exclusion appears in the grant. Noted but not flagged here: § 14.2 describes the Deliverable licence as \"revocable, non-transferable\" and limited to the Order Form term. That language is substantially constrained by § 13.3 (no revocation absent uncured material breach; transfer to Affiliate/successor permitted), § 14.3 (embedded Vendor Technology carries the § 13.2 perpetual licence) and § 10.1 (rights in accepted Deliverables survive). The residual issue is Vendor's ownership of Customer-specific Deliverables, which belongs to the IP-ownership rule rather than being duplicated under the licence-scope rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-00a4a55e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"The duplicate-numbered § 12.4 (p0046) imposes a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months on Customer covering any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory, with no carve-outs — walk-away territory under the rule and a failure of the fallback on scope, duration and carve-outs. It also contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. The smallest operative cure at the preferred level is flipping the prohibitory operator (\"shall not\" to \"may\"), which leaves no non-compete and no field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer while keeping every other word intact; a narrowed term-only restriction on a single named product is offered in the comment only. The separate no-hire covenant at p0045 is left for the applicable no-hire rule.","proposal":"Turn the 24-month, all-territory non-compete on Customer into a permission by changing \"shall not\" to \"may\".","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-ec7457dd","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 is the only provision giving Vendor audit rights over us (Section 23 contains no operative text). It matches the preferred position on all material terms: frequency limited to once per twelve months, thirty days' prior written notice, normal business hours, off-site where practicable, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1); Vendor bears costs unless underpayment exceeds five percent (22.2); and Vendor and its auditor are expressly barred from direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, and other suppliers' confidential information (22.2). Section 22.3 additionally protects findings as our Confidential Information. No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-8543a675","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match obligation on us, the Customer: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term, and comparison methodology, so it falls short of the fallback (defined product, 12 months, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore flip the mandatory operator so no MFN obligation burdens Customer, leaving the rest of the sentence intact; no Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere to preserve.","proposal":"Negate the Customer-side MFN/match obligation in Section 7.2.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mincommit-b4ab0b09","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment on us expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — the playbook's walk-away position, since there is no reduction or exit and no termination-for-convenience right elsewhere. It also fails the fallback, which would confine the commitment to the current 12-month term, make it reducible on 30 days' notice, and settle shortfalls by true-up rather than penalty, and it contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer \"has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.\" The redline takes the preferred position with a minimal in-sentence edit: no minimum quantity, and Services payable on a usage or ordered basis without take-or-pay obligation.","proposal":"No minimum commitment; Services payable on a usage or ordered basis only.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-renewal-efa4e44f","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"The renewal mechanic sits at the preferred position: renewals are for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (well inside the 30-day preferred window), and Vendor must send a reminder sixty days before renewal — with the extra Customer-favourable feature that a missed reminder extends the opt-out deadline to thirty days after receipt. § 8.3 caps renewal uplifts at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred cap, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and excludes prepaid periods. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the draft MSA against the playbook and identified **18 findings: 8 compliant, 7 deviations and 3 missing clauses**. The risk allocation is unusually mixed: the Vendor-facing protections we care most about are already strong, while the Customer-facing restrictions are aggressive and, in several places, internally contradictory.

What is already acceptable and needs no redline: limitation of liability (§21 — mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with a full carve-out set), assignment and change of control (§24 — unrestricted Customer assignment, Vendor bound asymmetrically in our favour), audit rights (§22), auto-renewal and the 30-day opt-out with a CPI/3% uplift cap (§8), warranties and remedies (§19), licence grant scope (§13), Vendor insurance (§18), and the absence of any Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties.

The problems cluster in two places. First, a set of one-sided restrictions on us — a three-year USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§2.1), a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both de facto exclusivity and an MFN against us (§7.2), a 24-month all-territory non-compete and an outright 24-month no-hire (both numbered §12.4) — each of which is contradicted by §12.3, where the Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. Second, structural gaps: **there is no indemnification article at all** (the outline runs from §19 to §21, while §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 each assume one exists, and §9.3 cross-references a non-existent "Section 20.5"), no termination-for-convenience right for Customer in a three-year committed term, and no transition-assistance or data-return/deletion obligation. Governing law is also internally inconsistent: §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts while §28.2 vests exclusive jurisdiction in New York County, New York.

Drafting note: proposed redlines have been generated and verified for all items below except **GOVLAW (§28.1/28.2)** and **NOSOLICIT (§12.4)**, where the automated edit did not pass verification. Those two require manual drafting before we send comments.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§1.5, 21.2–21.4, 18.2) | Meets preferred position; no redline. |
| 2 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Meets preferred position in full; Vendor bound asymmetrically in our favour. |
| 3 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 (first clause so numbered) | De facto exclusivity/ROFR; fails fallback. Redline verified. |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | §27.3 (with §§7.3, 24.4, 8–10) | No Customer-payable LDs or penalties; take-or-pay handled under MINCOMMIT. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3, 14.3, 10.1) | Meets preferred position; §14.2 language addressed under IP. |
| 6 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (duplicate-numbered) | 24 months, any product, any territory, no carve-outs. Redline verified. |
| 7 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Matches preferred position on all material terms. |
| 8 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better third-party terms. Redline verified. |
| 9 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | **Deviation** | §2.1 | USD 2m/year for three years, take-or-pay, no reduction or exit. Redline verified. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | Preferred position; missed-reminder extension runs in our favour. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, 6.2) | Meets or exceeds preferred position; disclaimer is mutual and carved back. |
| 12 | Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 (conflicts with §28.2) | Singapore law/exclusive Singapore courts; outside accepted set. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| 13 | Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No §20; see §19.5 and cross-refs at §§9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5 | No indemnity article at all; §9.3 cross-reference is broken. Insertion drafted and verified. |
| 14 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | Meets preferred position; cyber/privacy at USD 5m. |
| 15 | Low | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 (with §§14.1, 14.3, 14.4) | Vendor owns all Deliverables; Customer gets revocable term licence. Fails preferred and fallback. Redline verified. |
| 16 | Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 | One-way outright no-hire, all employees, 24 months, no carve-outs. **Redline verification failed — manual drafting required.** |
| 17 | Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (only §§9.1–9.3, 9.5; no §9.4) | No Customer convenience right in a three-year committed term. Insertion drafted and verified. |
| 18 | Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.1 (with §16.5) | No transition duty; no data return or certified deletion; §16.5 defers to a non-existent §11. Insertion drafted and verified. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and should be presented to the Vendor as conditions of signature, not as negotiating preferences:

1. **§2.1 — take-or-pay minimum commitment.** USD 2,000,000 per year for three years, expressly "without reduction or termination rights," with no termination-for-convenience right elsewhere in the Agreement. Our position: no minimum quantity; Services payable on a usage or ordered basis.
2. **§7.2 — disclose-and-match obligation.** Operates simultaneously as exclusivity/right of first refusal (EXCLUSIVITY) and as an MFN against us (MFN): unlimited as to product, term and comparison methodology, with no exit for Vendor service or delivery failures. Our position: no disclosure or match obligation on Customer.
3. **§12.4 — non-compete.** 24 months post-term, any competing product or service, any territory, no carve-outs. Our position: no non-compete and no field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer.
4. **Missing indemnification article (§20).** No Vendor IP indemnity at all, and §9.3 cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5," which does not exist. Our position: insert §20 at the preferred level, including the §20.5 infringement remedies so the §9.3 cross-reference resolves.
5. **No Customer termination for convenience (§9).** Absence of any convenience right in a three-year term carrying a USD 2m annual commitment. Our position: new §9.4 — 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees; no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.
6. **§28.1 — governing law and venue.** Singapore law with exclusive Singapore jurisdiction is outside the accepted set (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and conflicts with §28.2's exclusive New York County jurisdiction.

Note for the business: items 1–3 are each directly contradicted by **§12.3**, in which the Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. That internal inconsistency is our strongest lever and we should lead with it.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Confirm the commercial mandate on §2.1** with the business owner before we send comments — whether we can accept any committed volume, and if so at what level and with what reduction mechanic. The rest of the package is legal-led; this one is not.
2. **Manually draft the two failed redlines** before circulation: (a) §28.1/28.2 — conform governing law to New York, delete the conflicting Singapore forum wording, and confine the §28.2 injunctive-relief carve-out to the New York County courts so that law and forum form one permitted pair; (b) §12.4 — narrow to a mutual 12-month non-solicit of personnel directly involved in the Services, striking the no-hire words and the "regardless of how the employee applies" sweep-up, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
3. **Raise the duplicate numbering and broken cross-references** as a clean-up point in the same round: two clauses numbered §7.2 and two numbered §12.4; the outline jumps from §19 to §21; §9.3 cites a non-existent §20.5; §16.5 defers to a non-existent §11; §23 has no operative text; and there is no §9.4. We should ask the Vendor to reissue a renumbered draft so our comments map cleanly.
4. **Send the verified redlines** for §§2.1, 7.2, 12.4 (non-compete), 14.2, and the three insertions (§9.4, §20, §10.3), each with a short \[Playbook\] comment stating the position and, where sensible, the fallback.
5. **Do not reopen** the compliant items (§§8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 27.3). They meet or exceed our preferred positions and there is no benefit to us in putting them back in play.
6. **Escalate** if the Vendor refuses on the walk-away items, particularly the missing indemnity and the take-or-pay/no-exit combination, which together leave us paying USD 6m over three years with no exit and no recourse for third-party IP claims."}
